content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to [company_name] programmable logic controllers and accidentally purchased an older [product_name] module without a built-in display for my small test project. I created a program using the latest [product_name] programming software, but it's not possible to upload the program to this controller due to compatibility issues. Is there a way to upload the program, or is firmware available? I'm confused at the moment. I'm connecting with a USB cable.

Hi, the [article_no] hardware you have is quite outdated. One question: Are you using a demo version of [product_name] programming software? If so, even with new hardware, you can't download programs. You need the full, paid version of the software—though updates are free. Once you're in version [version_no] of the programming tool, go to File > Properties > Hardware Type and select [article_no]. You'll also need a special USB cable for uploading to this older hardware. Do you have that cable? Let me know if you need more help.
Is the USB cable you're using an original one from [company_name]? Have you installed the necessary drivers for it? Also, is your [product_name] programming software a full version, or just the demo?
Thank you for your reply. I do have the full version of the programming software. Regarding the cable, I'm not sure if it's an original or aftermarket option.

Thanks for the response. It's the full software, and the USB cable seems to work for communicating with the controller. I haven't installed additional USB drivers and I'm unsure which ones would be needed. Same for firmware upgrades—I don't know which firmware to install. I mostly use software and controllers from other brands.
Whether the cable is original or third-party doesn't really matter. If the right drivers aren't installed, the cable simply won't work.

It would have helped if you mentioned that communication with the [product_name] module is working. That would save us some questions. Have you set the cable type and chosen the correct COM port in your interface properties?

The cable does function and communicates with the controller. The problem is that the hardware is so old that it won't accept my program—the error is related to parameters. With other controller brands, it's possible to update firmware on older units to make newer programs work. I'm trying to find out if [company_name] supports something similar, but I couldn't find any firmware updates.
Communication works through USB. When I select the older controller version and try uploading the program, I get a parameter error.
When I select the controller, there's an error on the F1 key. And when I attempt to load the program, a second error appears.
The error says that the selected [product_name] module in your programming software doesn't match your actual device.
Please upload your project as a ZIP file to the forum.

You've selected the wrong [product_name] module in the hardware settings. Unfortunately, you can't choose the correct one because your program includes functions that the [article_no] can't support. For example, the F1 key is for an external display that only newer [product_name] controllers support. There are also flags, like M33, unavailable on such old devices. In other words, the [article_no] hardware is too outdated for your program.

Next time, before buying [product_name] hardware, you can press F2 while using the programming software to open the status window—it gives useful information like missing signals or which hardware is needed. If you know which controller you'll use, set that version in the software before programming; unsupported function blocks will disappear and transferring your program should be straightforward.
I made some changes to help the program run on [article_no]: - Changed F1 key to C1 key. - Added message text for the C1 cursor key. - Adjusted some flag block numbers.
Thank you. I will update later after trying your suggestions.
Thanks to everyone for your help. Next time, I will be more careful when buying hardware.

analysis.insight_summary: The user encountered compatibility issues when trying to upload a program created with newer [product_name] software to a considerably older [product_name] controller without a display. Communication via USB works, but upload fails with a parameter error. The user is uncertain about firmware compatibility, the need for original cables, and driver installations, hoping for backward compatibility or firmware updates similar to what other brands offer. Multiple contributors confirmed these problems are expected with such old hardware.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to upload and run new [product_name] programs on outdated [product_name] controllers, possibly through firmware updates, and is seeking detailed guidance on the required hardware and drivers for basic programming tasks.
